title: Let go, and it flies off straight
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 180" role="img" aria-label="A stone whirled in a circle flies off along the tangent when released" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><circle cx="120" cy="95" r="50" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><path d="M120,95 L158.3,62.9"/><circle cx="158.3" cy="62.9" r="5" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M158.3,62.9 L203.3,116.5" class="u" stroke-width="2"/><text x="232" y="150" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">path after release</text><text x="120" y="112" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">hand</text></svg>
back: A whirled stone leaves along the tangent, the line that just touches the circle. Tangent comes from the Latin for 'to touch'.

title: Tangent ⟂ radius
back: At the point of contact the radius meets the tangent at 90°. It is the shortest distance from the centre to the line.

title: Two tangents from one point
back: PA = PB. OP bisects the angle APB and the angle AOB.

title: Length of a tangent
back: The line to the centre is the hypotenuse.

title: How many tangents?
back: And a circle has infinitely many tangents in all, one at each point.

title: Proof: PA = PB
tex: \begin{gathered}\text{join }OA,\ OB,\ OP\\ \downarrow\\ 90^\circ,\ OA=OB,\ OP\text{ common}\\ \downarrow\\ \text{RHS}\Rightarrow PA=PB\end{gathered}
back: The congruence rule is RHS, not SAS.

title: Angle between two tangents
back: Quadrilateral OAPB has two right angles, so the other two add to 180°.

title: Quadrilateral around a circle
back: Equal tangents from each vertex give AB + CD = AD + BC.

title: Triangle around a circle
back: Mark AD = AF = x, BD = BE = y, CE = CF = z; each side is a sum of two letters.

title: Chord touching the inner circle
back: Pythagoras gives half the chord: remember to double.
